title: Mark, looking back
hook: the breathless gospel that ended in trembling
tomorrow: two houses, same street, same sermon. why does one fall?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the practices, and the ones that moved in: what stayed. Today, a Gospel in a hurry, and the strange place it lands.

Very early on the first day of the week, three women walk to a tomb carrying spices: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. All the way there they've been asking each other who will roll the stone away. When they look up, it's already rolled back. Inside, on the right, sits a young man in a long white garment. What he tells them sends them running out into the morning, shaking, and saying nothing to anyone. That's where Mark's Gospel ends.
screen: `THREE WOMEN, SPICES, DAWN.` → `THE STONE, ALREADY ROLLED.` → `THEY RAN, AND SAID NOTHING.`

segments.voice: Here's what the young man said: “But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.” And Peter, the one who had denied him, is named on purpose. Then the line readers keep coming back to: “And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.” Why end a gospel there? Some readers hear the book stop right at that verse; others read on into the verses printed after it. Either way, verse eight is worth sitting with. Mark doesn't do slow. No birth story, no family tree, and one word piling up: straightway. Straightway out of the water, straightway they left their nets. And here's the detail to tell a friend: his first verse is a title, “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.” The beginning. So some readers hear the trembling ending as a door back to the start. He goeth before you into Galilee: back where it all began, by the lake and the nets, out in ordinary life. Jesus isn't waiting at the tomb. He's already ahead. Mark gives fear an honest place on Easter morning, and the promise still stands.
screen: `TELL HIS DISCIPLES, AND PETER.` · `FOR THEY WERE AFRAID.` · `THE BEGINNING OF THE GOSPEL.` · `BACK TO GALILEE.` · then, large: `HE GOES BEFORE YOU.`

segments.voice: Say the young man's words out loud, slowly: he goeth before you. Then sit with the last line, for they were afraid, and let both be true at once. If you pray, bring one fear of your own and set the promise down beside it.
Mark. The breathless Gospel that begins with a title and ends with trembling women and a promise: he goes ahead.
Your line: he goes before you. Afraid and promised, both on the same morning. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1758 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 7 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: TWO HOUSES, SAME STREET, SAME SERMON. WHY DOES ONE FALL?`

howItsDone: Christians read Mark's Gospel in worship and at home; some read it straight through in one sitting, and some linger over its sudden ending at 16:8.

fork.setup: your friend got frightening news about her dad and hasn't told anyone, because she can't find words. what does Mark's ending suggest?
options: her silence means she's failing; she has to speak today.
fear and silence can be part of the story; the promise stands, and words can come later.
she should keep it to herself for good; some news is never shared.
fork.reveal: Mark ends with trembling women who said nothing, for they were afraid, and the promise was still true: he goeth before you.

original.note: the Greek for 'goeth before' in Mark 16:7: he leads the way ahead.

chat.says: on campus. it's huge and nobody knows me. i walked out of the info session shaking. is that bad?
options: Not bad. Mark's Easter ends with women trembling, and still: he goes before you.
Yes. If God wanted you there, you'd already feel totally at peace about it.
Ignore it. Real faith means never feeling afraid of anything at all.
chat.meaning: Mark gives fear an honest place on Easter morning, and the promise still stands: he goeth before you. Trembling and trust can share a day.

Salome.meaning: one of the women who came to the tomb

Galilee.meaning: the northern region where Jesus first called his friends

straightway.meaning: the King James word for at once, immediately

Mary Magdalene.meaning: a follower of Jesus who came to the tomb
